nodes.label: PBD and Turned-Profile Architecture
nodes.rationale: PBD already provides grid hashing and bitonic sorting, while a rotational R(y) profile gives an exact, cheap, bake-free, open-top cavity that follows the flask Transform and also yields a volume-to-height curve.

nodes.label: Turned-Profile Cavity Collision
nodes.rationale: Rotational symmetry makes the hollow top-open vessel exact and inexpensive without an SDF bake; following the vessel Transform naturally turns tilting into pouring.

nodes.label: Shared Multi-Liquid Solver Architecture
nodes.rationale: One FluidSolver and one FluidBody buffer let all liquids push and mix with one another while paying for only one bitonic sort; per-liquid scripts retain properties but do not own solvers.

nodes.label: Per-Particle Substance Index
nodes.rationale: A substance index lets a shared physical buffer select per-liquid color and emission now and later supports per-particle mass for real density layering.

nodes.label: Render-Only Fluid Feature
nodes.rationale: The render feature is deliberately data- and logic-free: it consumes CPU-registered buffers and draws them, leaving simulation, ownership, and orchestration elsewhere.

nodes.label: World-Space Particle Spawn
nodes.rationale: Sampling inside the flask in world space and appending to a shared FluidBody keeps particles independent of the flask; only the collider header follows the Transform.

nodes.label: Layer-Contact Despawn
nodes.rationale: Layer-tagged contact turns drains and discard surfaces into a general despawn mechanism: CPU gathers colliders, GPU marks particles dead, and Graveyard removes them from active rendering.

nodes.label: Milliliters-per-Particle Radius Coupling
nodes.rationale: Particle radius must derive from milliliters per particle and packing factor so small laboratory volumes use smaller particles and their visible level matches calibrated volume.

nodes.label: Group Frustum Render Culling
nodes.rationale: Culling liquid groups by AABB avoids off-screen draw cost while every particle continues to exist and simulate; per-particle culling would add unnecessary overhead.

nodes.label: CPU / GPU / Render Responsibility Split
nodes.rationale: GPU compute performs physics, CPU components own properties and orchestration, and a separate GPU render path only consumes registered buffers.

nodes.label: Bitonic MIN_ELEMENTS Floor
nodes.rationale: The 8192-element sort floor dominates small-volume performance and forces mostly inert padding particles, so reducing or adapting it is a primary optimization target.

nodes.label: Hollow Glassware Profile Collision
nodes.rationale: A turned GlasswareProfile preserves an open hollow vessel in the collider world, whereas using a MeshCollider for the flask would behave like a solid bounding box.

nodes.label: Moving-Collider Friction
nodes.rationale: Relative-velocity friction lets moving colliders drag fluid without accelerating it past the collider, while stationary colliders still allow sliding.

nodes.label: Dead-Particle Buffer Compaction
nodes.rationale: Periodic compaction truly shrinks buffers after kill-on-contact instead of merely hiding particles in Graveyard.

nodes.label: SDF Arbitrary-Mesh Collision
nodes.rationale: SDF collision is more general but remains postponed because baking was fragile and heavy; a later soft-push attempt leaked under PBD pressure and was reverted at the user's request.

nodes.label: SPH Box-Bound Simulation
nodes.rationale: The SPH alternative was rejected because its compute shader hard-clamps particles to an AABB, scales as O(n²), runs slowly, supports one color, and cannot model free flask-to-flask pouring.

nodes.label: LabLiquidVR Fake Surface
nodes.rationale: LabLiquidVR is validated and VR-ready but remains separate because its fake level and jet do not constitute independent free liquid.

nodes.label: Adaptive Rest Damping
nodes.rationale: Speed-dependent damping is strong near rest so the liquid settles, but weak during pouring so the jet remains lively.

nodes.label: s_corr Cohesion
nodes.rationale: The experimental cohesion term is disabled by default because with two solver iterations and CFL clamping it injected energy, saturated the clamp, and created a perpetual approximately 0.30 m/s limit cycle.

nodes.label: Particle Velocity Tint and Fresnel
nodes.rationale: Whitening fast particles suggests foam while a Fresnel rim gives a wet edge, improving the temporary particle-rendered liquid appearance.

nodes.label: uGUI Lab Panel
nodes.rationale: A scene uGUI panel replaces the unreliable F1 IMGUI panel and exposes damping, viscosity, cohesion, test actions, FPS, volume, and velocity; the missing EventSystem was the prior failure cause.

nodes.label: Grid Hash Full-Table Clearing
nodes.rationale: ClearTable must dispatch over every hash cell rather than every particle; stale un-cleared cells produced invalid neighbor bounds, near-2^31 loops, GPU TDR, freezes, and BSODs.

nodes.label: Normalized XSPH Viscosity
nodes.rationale: Replacing the unnormalized ViscLapKernel weight with normalized Poly6 keeps the XSPH blend bounded by viscosity and invariant to particle scale, preventing velocity feedback blow-up.

nodes.label: Spiky Gradient Epsilon Guard
nodes.rationale: Clamping r to an epsilon before p/r prevents coincident compressed particles from producing 0/0 NaNs that propagate through the simulation.

nodes.label: Cavity-Clamp Glassware Resolution
nodes.rationale: Clamping directly to the semi-infinite interior cavity and floor removes thin-shell tunneling and gradient NaNs while preserving an open top for pouring.

nodes.label: Boundary Particles
nodes.rationale: Boundary particles can supply pressure support that a soft SDF push lacks, but inert bitonic padding must not accidentally become an invisible physical floor.

nodes.label: Mass-Scale Calibration
nodes.rationale: An empirical massScale of four compensates for missing wall density support at the current radius and smoothing length so the fluid forms a stable column instead of a one-millimeter pancake.

nodes.label: Collider Transform Follow Smoothing
nodes.rationale: Rate-limited collider position, rotation, and maximum push convert Transform teleports into gradual motion, preserving liquid independence and avoiding velocity spikes while retaining slow-tilt pouring.

nodes.label: FlaskFluidTest Scene
nodes.rationale: Current-state and validation sections describe the scene as built, saved, and validated, despite an older inventory line later in the document still saying no FlaskFluidTest scene existed.

nodes.label: PBDFluid_SSF_Liquid Material Authority
nodes.rationale: A single material owns SSF color, absorption, Fresnel, opacity, and related appearance; FlaskFluidTest only wires buffers and simulation, and distinct liquids use duplicated materials rather than copied script fields.

nodes.label: Particle ShadowCaster
nodes.rationale: The cube proxy never casts a shadow; a separate ShadowsOnly particle draw reuses the GPU buffer and indirect draw so shadows follow the liquid rather than resurrecting an invisible box.

nodes.label: Screen-Space Transparency Limitation
nodes.rationale: SSF refraction depends on its screen-space buffers and the URP opaque texture, so transparent objects rendered later cannot appear in the liquid's refraction; caustics and spectral colored shadows are also absent.
